# SuperPilot by Superleap
## PM Assignment Submission — Dilith Dinesh

This is a product feature proposal and interactive prototype submitted as a
take-home assignment for the Product Manager role at Superleap AI CRM.

---

## What This Is

A fully interactive prototype demonstrating SuperPilot — a proposed AI feature
for Superleap CRM that gives B2B sales teams institutional memory across the
entire deal lifecycle.

The prototype functions as both a product marketing page and a working CRM demo.
It is not a production application. All data is fictional and illustrative.

---

## The Assignment

Sector: B2B
Industry: SaaS / Technology
End user: Account Executive (B2B SaaS sales rep)

Brief: Design an AI-powered feature inside Superleap CRM that increases
the productivity of the end user by cutting low-value work so they can
focus on what drives revenue.

---

## The Problem Identified

B2B SaaS deals involve 6+ role handoffs over a 6-12 week sales cycle:
SDR → AE → Solutions Engineer → Legal → Implementation → CSM.

At every handoff, institutional memory leaks. Commitments made in week 2
are forgotten by the implementation team in week 8. The prospect remembers
every conversation. The selling team starts from scratch at every transition.

Beyond handoffs, sales reps waste 2+ hours daily on:
- Pre-call context reconstruction: 12 min per call, manually stitching
  together emails, call notes, and CRM history
- Post-call administration: 15 min per call — logging, tasks, follow-up draft

The data to fix this already exists in Gmail, VoIP systems, Google Meet,
and the CRM pipeline. The problem is no system synthesizes it into memory.

Quantified baseline:
- 60% of rep time is non-selling (Salesforce State of Sales 2026)
- 18% of the average week is manual data entry
- 32% of reps spend 1+ hour per day on data entry alone
- Teams average 8-10 standalone tools with no unified context layer
- 46% of sales pros say data quality issues directly hurt their sales

---

## The Feature: SuperPilot

Superleap already captures every call, email, and meeting your reps have.
SuperPilot is how Superleap turns that data into context, actions, and memory —
automatically, for every rep, on every deal.

It is not a standalone product. It is not a bolt-on tool. It is how Superleap
works harder for the rep — reading what is already captured, synthesizing it,
and surfacing the right context at the right moment. No new tools. No new
workflows. Superleap getting smarter.

### Four core capabilities:

1. PRE-CALL BRIEF
   Before every call, SuperPilot assembles a contextual brief from emails,
   call transcripts, meeting notes, and deal history. The rep reads it in
   60 seconds and walks in knowing everything — last touchpoint, open
   commitments, stakeholder map, suggested focus.
   Time saved: 12 min → 1 min per call.

2. POST-CALL INTELLIGENCE
   When a call ends, SuperPilot reads the transcript and automatically:
   - Logs a structured call summary
   - Creates tasks with suggested due dates
   - Detects cross-functional dependencies and tags the right team
   - Drafts the follow-up email
   Time saved: 15 min → 2 min per call.

3. PROACTIVE DEAL MONITORING
   Watches every active deal for risk signals — not on a timer, but
   contextually. Surfaces specific, actionable nudges in the rep's
   morning feed. Not "5 days since last activity" — but "proposal
   opened 4 times, no response, CFO not engaged, call today."

4. HANDOFF BRIEFS
   When a deal changes hands (AE → Implementation, AE → CSM),
   SuperPilot auto-generates: why they bought, commitments made with
   source links, stakeholder map, watch-outs, success metrics agreed.
   The new owner inherits everything. The customer never repeats themselves.

---

## Quantified ROI

Per rep per day (at 5 calls/day):
- Pre-call time saved:    11 min × 5 = 55 min
- Post-call time saved:   13 min × 5 = 65 min
- Total recovered:        ~2 hours/day = 25% of working day

For a 10-rep team:
- 20 hours of selling time recovered daily
- ~2.5 additional FTE equivalent selling capacity
- At ₹5L average deal, 8% conversion: ₹2.4Cr+ additional revenue/year
- New rep ramp: 3-4 months → 6-8 weeks (60% reduction)
- Post-call admin reduction: 87% (15 min → 2 min)
- Pre-call prep reduction: 92% (12 min → 1 min)

---

## Product Roadmap

V1 — WORKFLOW COMPRESSION (Ships now, works on existing data):
Pre-call brief, post-call extraction, follow-up email draft,
deal intelligence feed, handoff brief generation, deal memory.
No new integrations required. No new data collection.
Adoption is frictionless — value delivered through existing behavior.

V2 — PREDICTIVE INTELLIGENCE (Requires V1 data accumulation, Q2):
WhatsApp synthesis, stakeholder sentiment tracking, predictive deal
risk scoring (ML on historical patterns), manager team-level view,
Slack/Teams delivery, email thread AI interpretation.

V3 — CROSS-WORKSPACE ORCHESTRATION (Platform play, Q4):
Multi-rep deal memory, competitive intelligence signals, revenue
forecasting from memory signals, SuperPilot API, MCP integration,
cross-org benchmarks.

---

## Go-To-Market Strategy

### ICP
B2B companies, 20-200 employees, 5-30 rep sales teams, 4-12 week
sales cycles, ₹3L-₹50L average deal value, currently on HubSpot or
Salesforce, 6+ tools in stack, Series A to Series C.

Buying signals: reps complaining about admin, deals going cold after
proposal stage, onboarding failures traced to missing AE documentation,
new rep ramp taking 3+ months.

### Wedge Strategy
Land with the AE (primary pain owner, immediate measurable value) →
Expand to full sales team (manager adopts for pipeline reviews) →
Deepen to CS and Implementation (handoff briefs prove value) →
Platform (RevOps, forecasting, V3 capabilities).

### Why Teams Switch from HubSpot/Salesforce
Not because of more features. Because CXOs are asking:
"Is our CRM AI-native?" HubSpot and Salesforce have AI features.
SuperPilot is AI-native. The data model, workflow, and intelligence
layer are designed together. That is the answer CXOs are looking for.

Additional switching drivers:
- No 6-9 month implementation (Superleap live in 30 days)
- India-native pricing vs $150-300/user/month Western enterprise cost
- WhatsApp-first architecture for Indian B2B workflows
- No bolt-on AI cost (Gong + Clari = $500+/user/year add-on stack)

### Pricing Logic
SuperPilot is priced as an add-on module per seat on top of base
Superleap plan. Not usage-based — per-seat, because value is continuous
and ambient, not transactional. The feature runs in the background
constantly. Per-seat pricing aligns the business model with the
product experience.

### Competitive Moat
1. Data flywheel: every interaction processed improves intelligence
   accuracy. Indian B2B deal data compounds over time.
2. Native integration: no integration tax, no context switching,
   intelligence where the work happens.
3. Institutional memory lock-in: after 12+ months, the entire deal
   history and commitment trail lives in SuperPilot memory.
   Switching CRMs means losing that memory. Irreplaceable context
   is the most defensible moat in B2B SaaS.

---

## Industry Applicability

SuperPilot's core architecture — contextual summarization, entity
extraction, deal memory, proactive intelligence — is industry-agnostic.
What changes per vertical is the data sources and workflow surfaces.

B2B SaaS (primary vertical):
Pre-call brief + handoff briefs for 6-role deal lifecycle.
"2 hrs/day recovered per rep, 65% admin reduction."

EdTech / Education (B2C variant — Follow-up Re-entry Brief):
Before every follow-up call with a student lead, a 3-line card:
what was discussed, what objection was raised, what to lead with
based on exam proximity. 2-3 min prep × 40 follow-ups/day =
1.5-2 hrs saved per counsellor. 10-15 additional students reached daily.

BFSI / Lending:
Relationship managers with 20-40 active loan proposals.
Deal intelligence flags stalled proposals with specific context:
"proposal opened 3 times, promoter not yet contacted, day 6 of avg 8."

Real Estate:
Site visit context preserved across follow-up calls.
Buyer preference brief auto-generated. Inventory matching suggested.

Healthcare:
Patient coordinator context brief across multiple touchpoints.
Commitments made (insurance check, referral follow-up) tracked.
Patient never repeats their history.

---

## AI Architecture

### Three-layer architecture:

LAYER 1 — DATA INGESTION & UNIFICATION
Sources: Gmail API, VoIP webhooks (Ozonetel/Ameyo), Google Meet API,
Fathom webhooks, CRM native data, WhatsApp Business API (via Gallabox/Wati).
All normalized into a unified interaction timeline (JSON event objects).
Transcription: Deepgram (real-time, post-call) or Whisper (batch, cost-sensitive).

LAYER 2 — INTELLIGENCE ENGINE
Four AI components:

Component A — Contextual Summarization (Pre-Call Brief)
Model: Claude Sonnet | Temperature: 0.2 | Max tokens: 800
Input: Stored deal summary (cached) + last 3-5 raw interactions
Output: Structured JSON with source_event_id on every claim
Source links enable rep to verify any AI-generated statement.

Component B — Entity & Action Extraction (Post-Call Panel)
Model: Claude Sonnet | Temperature: 0.1 | Max tokens: 1000
Input: Full transcript with speaker labels + current deal state
Output: Action items, commitments, cross-functional tags, call summary
Cross-functional routing uses explicit intent map (not free-form inference).

Component C — Deal Intelligence Scoring (Deal Feed)
Hybrid: rule-based signal computation + LLM interpretation
Threshold gate prevents LLM calls on healthy deals (~80% of pipeline)
Cost impact: 180 → 36 LLM calls/day per workspace at 30 active deals.
Signals: days since activity, stage velocity ratio, proposal open count,
economic buyer engagement, overdue commitments, response rate.

Component D — Incremental Deal Memory (Foundation)
Delta summarization on every new interaction. Never reprocesses history.
Cost stays flat as deal history grows. Full version history maintained.
Schema: deal summary, commitments with verbatim quotes, recurring concerns,
stakeholder map, success metrics, open questions.

LAYER 3 — DELIVERY & SURFACING
Triggered: calendar event or deal record opened after 3+ days inactivity
Event-driven: call end webhook → post-call pipeline starts immediately
Scheduled: batch job every 6 hours for deal intelligence monitoring

### Orchestration:

Pattern 1 — Post-Call Processing
Sequential job queue (BullMQ/Celery). Latency-tolerant (2-3 min).
8-step pipeline: webhook → recording fetch → transcription → context
fetch → LLM extraction → CRM write → memory update → rep notification.
Each step independently retryable. Failures go to dead letter queue.

Pattern 2 — Pre-Call Brief
Parallel fan-out with 3-second hard timeout. Latency-critical (<10s).
5 sources fetched simultaneously: Gmail, VoIP, Meet/Fathom, CRM, Redis cache.
Graceful degradation: brief generates from available sources, labels missing ones.
Speed: parallel fetches + cached summary + Redis = consistently under 4 seconds.

Pattern 3 — Deal Intelligence Monitoring
Scheduled batch every 6 hours. Fan-out across all active deals (50 concurrent).
Threshold gate: rules first (cheap), LLM only for flagged deals (~20%).
Concurrency controlled for large workspaces. Overflow queues to next run.

### Technology Stack:
Job queue: BullMQ (Node) / Celery (Python)
Transcription real-time: Deepgram
Transcription batch: Whisper (self-hosted)
LLM: Claude Sonnet
Orchestration V1: Async/await + Promise.all
Orchestration V2: Temporal or LangGraph
Memory storage: PostgreSQL + JSONB
Cache: Redis
Scheduler: node-cron / Celery beat

### Production Constraints & Mitigations:
Data quality: degrades gracefully, labels missing sources, never fabricates
Latency: parallel fetching + cached summaries keeps pre-call under 4 seconds
Hallucination: every claim carries source_event_id with clickable verification link

---

## Why This Is A Superleap Feature, Not A Competing Product

The brief asks for an AI-powered feature inside Superleap CRM.
SuperPilot is exactly that — not a layer on top of Superleap,
but Superleap's own intelligence capabilities made visible and actionable.

Every data source SuperPilot reads from is already inside Superleap.
Every surface SuperPilot appears on is inside Superleap's UI.
Every action SuperPilot takes writes back to Superleap's data model.
There is no SuperPilot without Superleap. They are the same product.

Superleap already has:
- SuperFill: post-call notes (extends to all channels in SuperPilot)
- SuperSense: sentiment detection (extends across full deal lifecycle)
- Google Meet integration: pre-call context (extends to every call type)
- Gmail integration: email capture (AI interpretation layer added on top)
- VoIP integrations: Ozonetel, Ameyo, Twilio
- WhatsApp Business API: via Gallabox/Wati partner integrations
- 100+ tool integrations

SuperPilot is the connective tissue — the unified intelligence layer
that ties existing capabilities into one continuous workflow.
No new data infrastructure required for V1.
The data exists. It just hasn't been interpreted.

/crm/gtm — GTM: ICP, wedge, pricing, competitive positioning, expansion
/crm/industries — SuperPilot across B2B SaaS, EdTech, BFSI, Real Estate, Healthcare
/crm/architecture — AI architecture and orchestration technical deep dive

A guided tour auto-starts after login. 7 steps, covers all key
SuperPilot moments. Dismissible. Replayable from the header.

all SuperPilot features live including post-call panel, handoff brief,
transcript modal, and email draft.

---

## Honest Limitations

1. All data is fictional. No real CRM data used.
2. AI features are simulated — this is a UI prototype, not a working AI system.
3. Some CRM pages (Leads, Activities, Reports) are placeholder stubs.
4. Mobile layout not optimized. Best viewed at 1280px+.
5. The AI architecture is a design proposal, not a production implementation.
   Real implementation requires integration work with Superleap's infrastructure.
6. ROI numbers are modeled estimates based on published research (Salesforce
   State of Sales 2026) and reasonable assumptions — not from live product data.
